newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Foncier unions seek 1-yr stay, Paribas report.
newsitem.headline: Cr Foncier unions seek 1-yr stay, Paribas report.

text.p: Unions fighting to save French home loans group Credit Foncier said on Monday, the 10th day of a staff sit-in at the Paris headquarters, that they had several partnership ideas to put to mediator Philippe Rouvillois.

The unions also called on the government to release a report by Paribas for the Finance Ministry, saying the report was used for the latter's wind-down deliberations and released neither to Foncier chairman Jerome Meyssonnier, nor the National Assembly's finance commission.

The unions, which held a news conference to make their case against the government plan for a break-up and partial takeover by Credit Immobilier, said Foncier needed a partner and about a year to get back on its feet and could need as little as one billion or 1.5 billion francs in recapitalisation.
Michel Lamy, one of the main spokesmen for the cross-union grouping at Credit Foncier, said the group was likely to make a profit of one billion francs in 1997 after a similar forecast for 1996.

He and other union members accused the finance ministry of ignoring a well documented economic case to stick with a plan for the Credit Immobilier takeover and break-up and urged it to drop what amounted to "premeditated assassination".

The unions said their calculation of recapitalisation needs, far less than the eight billion francs suggested by Juppe in the Senate last week, included accounting for some 3.1 billion francs in latent capital gains in property which they said had not been taken into account so far.

The unions, presenting a joint front for 3,300 staff, said Credit Foncier had taken a 25 percent share of the market for zero interest and other low interest housing loans since the government abolished a near monopoly which Foncier had over another kind of cheap loan product for low income families.

Unions, who were due to meet Rouvillois on Monday afternoon, said they would not reveal their ideas on possible partnerships for the time being but that there were other ideas than the one for a link-up with Caisses d'Epargne savings bank grouping.
